segments.narration: Wedding cakes, coal wagons and a coffin all arrived uninvited. One London address. One morning in 1810. Nobody inside had ordered anything.
Fifty-four Berners Street belonged to a Mrs Tottenham. Chimney sweeps knocked at five in the morning. Then bakers, furniture vans, an organ.
By afternoon police had to block the street. The Duke of Gloucester turned up. So did the chairman of the Bank of England.
Who does this to a stranger? A twenty-two-year-old writer named Theodore Hook, for a one-guinea bet that he could make any address famous.
He had spent six weeks writing up to four thousand letters. Police offered a reward and never caught him. He confessed in a novel, twenty-five years later.
